corrections.label: Discount float noise collapsed
corrections.detail: Floating-point noise stored 0.15 as two distinct values (0.15 and 0.15000000000000002), splitting one discount level into two in every slicer and grouping. Values are rounded to 4dp, which removes the noise without disturbing any real rate.

corrections.label: Anomalous discount levels flagged, not altered
corrections.detail: Four levels (0.2%, 20.2%, 40.2%, 60.2%) look like a clean rate plus 0.002 and appear only on the 10% margin tier. They are left exactly as supplied — rewriting them would break the Profit reconstruction — and are surfaced as a data note.

corrections.label: US customer IDs de-duplicated
corrections.detail: US customer numbers carry a 9th digit encoding the US sub-region rather than the customer, inflating the US customer count roughly 3.2x. The trailing digit is stripped so one shopper is one customer.

corrections.label: Sudan region reassigned
corrections.detail: Sudan appeared under both North Africa and Eastern Africa. The 2 outlying rows were folded into North Africa, its dominant region.

corrections.label: Exact duplicate rows removed
corrections.detail: Two order lines were byte-for-byte duplicates of an existing line and would have double-counted their sales and profit.

corrections.label: Product name casing folded
corrections.detail: "REN Clean Skincare Moroccan Rose Otto Bath Oil" also appeared as "Ren …", counting one product as two.

limitations.label: No cost or COGS field exists
limitations.detail: Profit is supplied directly and resolves exactly to Sales x (BaseMargin - Discount) on every row, where BaseMargin is one of four tiers assigned per order line. Discount is therefore the only lever on margin, and no cost-driven metric is offered.

limitations.label: Base margin is an order-line attribute
limitations.detail: Eight of the seventeen subcategories price at a single margin tier; the other nine mix two, with no dimension in the workbook explaining the split. Breakeven discount is exact per line, but a subcategory-level breakeven is a revenue-weighted average and is labelled as such.

limitations.label: No SKU level exists
limitations.detail: The workbook stops at Product. The category hierarchy therefore drills Category -> Subcategory -> Product, with no SKU tier.

limitations.label: Category is an order-line attribute, not a product attribute
limitations.detail: 3576 products are recorded across multiple subcategories, so a product has no single category. Category and Subcategory are aggregated from order lines; product rankings are shown on their own or within a chosen category, never with a category label attached to the product.

limitations.label: No sub-segment field exists
limitations.detail: Segment has exactly 3 values and no child column. The segment drill-down therefore descends Segment -> Market -> Country -> Customer, which the data does support.

limitations.label: Sales is a gross, pre-discount figure
limitations.detail: Sales equals Quantity x unit price with the discount applied to Profit only. Both Gross and Net revenue are exposed, and every KPI states which basis it uses.

limitations.label: Weekday analysis is not offered
limitations.detail: Order dates were synthesised and the weekday distribution is degenerate (Thursday 990 rows against Tuesday 9,348). Year, quarter and month are sound; day-of-week is not, so no weekday visual exists.
